 The comparison you never see
 Your customers compare you before they ever ring 
 1 Today
 Your site was a one-off job a few years ago. It works, but it does not bring in work, and you are not sure how people find you now.
 2 Side by side
 Around Horsham, customers often search, compare two or three sites and ring one. A site that hides your services, areas or contact details loses that comparison without you knowing it happened.
 3 The site that gets the call
 A site that wins the comparison: clear services, the villages you cover, proof, a price guide and a quote form that takes a minute.
 A checklist to hold any site against
 What a good Horsham business website includes 
 These six points decide most side-by-side comparisons. Use them to judge your current site, or any quote you are weighing up.
 A first line that says what you do
 Your trade and your town belong at the top of the page, in plain words. Visitors comparing three tabs will not scroll to work out whether you do the job they need.
 A separate section for each service
 Each service needs its own clear description, because a list of everything you do tells nobody whether you do their job well. Search engines and AI assistants read those sections too.
 The villages you actually cover
 Naming Southwater, Billingshurst or Henfield settles the first question a customer has, which is whether you come to them. A vague line about the surrounding area does not.
 Proof from real work
 Photos of finished jobs and reviews from named customers do more than any claim about quality. When two sites look alike, the one showing evidence is the one that gets trusted.
 A price guide, even a rough one
 A starting figure saves the customer a phone call just to find out if you are in budget. Firms that publish one look more straightforward than the ones that say nothing.
 A quote form that takes a minute
 Ask only for a name, a contact and the job, and keep the phone number one tap away on a mobile. Every extra box is another reason to go back to the other tab.

 Questions worth asking any Horsham designer 
 Will you take on a firm in Southwater or Billingshurst?
 Yes, and wider West Sussex. Web design across West Sussex is the same service at the same published price, wherever the business is based.
 How do people find a local business online now?
 Through search, maps and AI assistants, and all three read the same clear facts about what you do and where. That is why these sites are built answer-first.
 What does a good Horsham business website need?
 Six things: a first line naming your trade and town, clear services, the villages you cover, proof from real jobs, a price guide and a short quote form. The section above goes through each one.
 What will a Horsham website cost me?
 Starter is £600 for 5 pages and Core is £995 for 8. Should you need more, each further page is £125. Hosting and care then runs at £10 a month.
 How quickly can it go live?
 Allow 1 to 3 weeks from the day your deposit lands. Sending your photos and business details early is the biggest thing you can do to keep it moving.
 Will I own it when it is done?
 You own the site once it is paid for.
 Which is the better fit, Starter or Core?
 Starter works when you offer a handful of services from one place. Core gives you room for separate service and area pages, which helps when customers are comparing you on a specific job.
 What do you need from me?
 Photos, your services, the areas you cover and any reviews you already have. Andy writes the words from there, so you are checking the copy instead of producing it.
 Will it work properly on a phone?
 Yes. Each site is designed for mobile first, since a customer comparing local firms is often doing it on a phone.
 How much search work comes with the build?
 The technical SEO and schema are set up in every site, so Google can read it from launch. Regular monthly SEO is a separate service and is not part of the build price.
 Can I add an AI receptionist later?
 Yes. It is an add-on from £497 to set up and from £97 a month, and nothing about your website has to be rebuilt to take it.
 Why do you publish your prices?
 Because you are probably comparing several designers, and a figure you can see saves everyone a conversation that goes nowhere.
